newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Stagecoach mulls Auckland buses - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Stagecoach mulls Auckland buses - paper.

text.p: Stagecoach Holdings Plc, Britain's fast-growing bus and rail company, is mulling a bid for a bus company in Auckland, New Zealand, the Financial Times said on Monday.

As expansion opportunities dwindle in Britain, the aggressive company has turned its attention to the Pacific Rim, including Australia and Vietnam, and might explore joint ventures when the Chinese market opens up, the newspaper said. Auckland's Yellow Bus Company, which is being sold by the Auckland Regional Services Trust, could be worth 30-40 million pounds on annual revenues of 30 million.
The newspaper quoted chairman Brian Souter as saying Stagecoach would be interested in bidding for the Yellow Bus company.
